prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1135; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound on a multi-lane roadway in Katy, Texas, when the vehicle ahead slowed for traffic. Driver 1 reported that the vehicle stopped suddenly and was struck from behind by Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 2 acknowledged that they did not stop in time and admitted following too closely. Independent witnesses at the scene described the impact the same way, and photographs taken on scene are consistent with a rear-end collision. Passenger was seated in the rear of Driver 1's vehicle and was confirmed present by responding officers and witnesses. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash and was transported to a local medical facility for evaluation. The injury complaint is plausible given the nature of the impact. Damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle is visible, but it is not clear from the scene whether all of the damage resulted from this impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is known to the reporting officer. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
